Hi Alex —

Thanks again for a productive demo today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so Procurement and Security have a clean handoff: 

What we covered
- Demo: low-latency inference for payment orchestration, structured logging, and streaming responses for webhook pipelines.
- Typical customer footprint: inference endpoints + prefix/KV caching + logging to a managed store.

Primary asks (please):
1) Please complete the attached security questionnaire (GreenSky_Security_Questionnaire_v1.xlsx) with your initial answers — this lets our compliance team map evidence quickly.
2) Share a current network/systems diagram (VPC boundaries, gateways, PII stores) — the sample diagram format is attached (greenSky_network_diagram_v2.pdf).
3) Confirm scope: who is the economic buyer and who will own security signoff (probable contacts: Priya Shah for Procurement, Matt Gomez for Security?).
4) Target timeline: security kickoff week of Nov 29. If that works, we can lock a 60-minute working session.

Suggested kickoff agenda:
- Introductions & scope definition (systems in/out of scope)
- Questionnaire walkthrough & evidence list
- Minimal data flow diagram review
- Procurement redline/prelim terms (if ready)

I attached the questionnaire and an example network diagram to this thread and put a copy in the shared Drive for easy collaboration: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1gk-ExampleDriveLink

Ben Carter (cc'd) will be the primary account owner handling procurement logistics; Jordan Blake will join the kickoff for technical deep-dive.

If you prefer, send the first-pass questionnaire back and we’ll pre-populate evidence requests before the call.

Best,

Thanks Alex — this is perfect context. A few clarifications to make the kickoff efficient: 

In-scope systems (proposed)
- Payment processing layer (GreenSky API/Gateway) that sends transaction payloads to Redwood inference endpoints.
- Any storage that contains customer PII or transaction-level data that Redwood would see/receive (logs, debug captures, analytics raw buckets).
- Webhook endpoints that receive model-enriched payloads (we need to review signing and backpressure behavior).
- Third-party processors only when they receive raw, identifiable customer data from GreenSky (if they only receive aggregated telemetry, they are out-of-scope).

Agenda (60–75m)
- Intro + final scope decision (10m)
- Walk through the questionnaire answers and flag missing evidence (25m)
- Network diagram + minimal data flow review (15m)
- Procurement/terms next steps & owners (10–15m)

Action items for GreenSky before kickoff
- Confirm Matt/Greg who will own the technical evidence (we'll need access to SOC2 report links or equivalent)
- Confirm whether third-party processors (analytics vendors) store raw transactions — if yes, name them and we’ll include them in evidence requests
- Confirm Priya as econ buyer so Ben can prepare commercial outline and brief SOW redline (I attached our SOW_redline_template.docx for reference).

Ben and Jordan are copied to coordinate logistics and the working session invite. I’ll also put the questionnaire + diagrams into our shared Drive folder and create an evidence checklist ahead of the call: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1gk-ExampleDriveLink

Proposed kickoff: Tue, 30 Nov 2026 at 09:30 PT (tentative). Please reply with confirmations or a preferred alternate.

Thanks —

Kimberly Park
